Senses.Explanation: Literally, the entire body. The term occurs 1,418 times in 299 allowlisted texts and ranges grammatically from a noun ('fall short of the whole') to an extent expression ('entirely is the pearl'); these describe the same thing as a complete whole rather than different referents. Its characteristic Chan collocations make that whole 'appear' (378 hits in 174 texts) or be 'exposed' (153 in 95). Xuansha's pearl exchange says, 'the whole body is the pearl—who else would you have recognize it?' Teaching-seat verses pair a raised whisk, staff, dust mote, or opened sleeve with the whole body's appearing.
Senses.Note: The different grammatical placements do not warrant a split: noun, modifier, and extent readings all designate completeness of the same referent. The deviation lies in the recurring public formulas 'the whole body appears' (全體現) and 'the whole body is exposed' (全體露), not in an imported claim about a metaphysical 'total reality.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 既是一顆明珠，學人為甚不識？沙曰：全體是珠，更教誰識？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷). Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Ciyun Yanlong section raising Xuansha's pearl exchange. Xuansha Shibei is the exact quoted speaker who answers that the whole body is the pearl and asks who else could be made to know it; Ciyun Yanlong is the later raiser.

Occurrences.Kwic: 極目青天無片雲，萬象森羅全體露。若也擬議更商量，特地翻成箇露布。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷). Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Kaixian Zhixun section. Kaixian Zhixun is the exact hall speaker who says that the myriad forms are exposed in their entirety beneath a clear sky without a patch of cloud.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉拂子云。盧舍本身全體現。當機直下沒纖毫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 圓悟佛果禪師語錄. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact actor: he raises the whisk and says 盧舍本身全體現.

Occurrences.Kwic: 驀拈拄杖云：「龍袖拂開全體現，象王行處絕狐蹤。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 密雲禪師語錄, fifteenth-day hall address. Miyun Yuanwu is the exact speaker: abruptly raising his staff, he says that when the dragon sleeve brushes open the whole body appears and where the elephant king walks fox tracks cease.

Occurrences.Kwic: 當機微笑，窺見一斑；依位無言，猶虧全體。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 天界覺浪盛禪師全錄, public exchange in Juelang Daosheng's record. The exact speaker is an unnamed questioning monk: in the stored advance (進云), he says that a timely smile reveals only one patch and that silence according with one's station still falls short of the whole. The six-rung review found no personal name for this monk.
